findings.text: follow-on: the base arm ran an earlier revision of the new test file than the head arm did -- the manifest's baseline_suite names only two of the final file's three unserved cases (test_a_picker_fallback_to_an_unserved_backend_refuses and test_a_picker_route_to_an_unserved_backend_refuses_and_names_it), not test_a_picker_refusal_checks_the_unserved_default, which was added with the second fix. Re-running the final test file against the base tree independently reds that third case too (4 failed / 4 passed at base vs 8 passed at head), so the reproduction holds; the recorded red arm simply under-covers the final test file by one id. Evidence-fidelity note, not a defect in the fix.

follow-on: on the live picker path cli.py now calls dispatch_picker_selection with no records/verdict_inputs/budget_snapshot, so the pick builds its own ledger/verdict/budget inputs (reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py builds rows when records is None) where dispatch() previously built and passed them with per-input error capture. The result is equivalent for a healthy ledger and the picker's own except still records a fallback reason, so this is a relocation rather than a regression, but the picker may now depend on pick()'s default input resolution rather than the dispatcher's, which is worth recording beside the one-pick contract.

item_verdicts.diff: read 8a81c011d against 47da2dc0a: 107 added lines in reckon/cli.py introduce _picker_routed_backend and thread a picker_selection through _model_availability_refusal and crew_dispatch so the deterministic availability probe runs on the backend the picker resolved; 68 lines in reckon/crew/dispatch.py make dispatch() accept and reuse the caller's picker_selection instead of asking again; plus a 324-line new test file and the evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when is that a picker-routed dispatch still refuses a model the account does not serve; an independent re-run of the final test file plus the pre-existing echo test reproduces base 4 failed / 4 passed (EXIT=1) and head 8 passed (EXIT=0), and the reviewed run's own named gate is 53 passed EXIT=0 at a534e5370.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal under plan §6 is that a picker-routed dispatch still refuses a model the account does not serve; the change asks the picker once and applies the same deterministic availability probe to the backend the selection resolves (route, fallback, refuse and route-without-backend all reaching the backend the dispatch really uses), so the picker route can no longer dispatch to a backend the deterministic route would refuse.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, baseline_suite 3 failed at 8a81c011d and after_suite 0 failed at a534e5370, negative-control.log 2 failed/1 passed EXIT=1, commits 63c1e61b0/57a92ecef/a534e5370/47da2dc0a, declared changed_paths include reckon/crew/dispatch.py under the coordinator's explicit grant.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed diff touches reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/dispatch.py, tests/test_picker_route_keeps_availability_refusal.py and the evidence fragment; dispatch.py lies outside the node's declared scope but the coordinator's resume advice explicitly grants it ('You may now write reckon/crew/dispatch.py ... the coordinator accepts it at promotion') bounded to the dispatch() pick call site and its signature, which the diff observes.

justifications.durability: the change is pinned by five new cases (fallback-to-unserved exits 5, route-to-unserved names the backend and exits 5, refuse-to-unserved-default exits 5, route-to-served previews, and a two-answer mock picker proves one call per dispatch with the dispatched backend equal to the checked one), plus a recorded red control restoring availability_refusal = None (2 failed/1 passed, EXIT=1); every commit carries a conventional subject and a body.
justifications.evidence: base reproduces -- an independent re-run of the final test file plus the pre-existing echo test gives 4 failed / 4 passed at 8a81c011d (EXIT=1) and 8 passed at head (EXIT=0), so the defect and its fix are both reproduced; both arm logs carry the module-identity and cwd header lines the prior node's were missing; the negative control records EXIT=1 with the two unserved ids. The cut: the recorded base arm predates the final refuse case, so it reds two of the three unserved cases rather than three.
justifications.fit: comments state the mechanism and its reason without plan, sprint or ticket identifiers or author attribution; the four commits are conventional with bodies and no AI trailer; the one naming-check hit is the test fixture's own <meta name="plan-slug"> data value; ruff adds zero findings on all three changed files (cli.py 4->4, dispatch.py 7->7, new test 0).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the goal is met exactly as the brief required: a picker-routed dispatch now runs the deterministic model-availability refusal on the backend the picker resolves, so a route or fallback to an unserved backend exits 5 (named) and a route to a served backend still dispatches, while a hold resolves no lane and is left to the picker's own hold path; the base/head re-run reproduces the defect at base and the fix at head.
justifications.scope_discipline: the reviewed diff changes only reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/dispatch.py, the new test file and the evidence fragment; no plan, sprint or index state was mutated, and the worker left the node unclosed. The single out-of-scope path, reckon/crew/dispatch.py, is edited under an explicit coordinator grant quoted in the run's resume advice and held to the grant's bound (the dispatch() pick call site and its signature), so it is an authorised extension rather than an unchecked write.
